era5_land_monthly_global.source: Copernicus C3S Climate Data Store — ERA5-Land monthly averaged data from 1950 to present (Muñoz Sabater 2019), doi:10.24381/cds.68d2bb30; variables: total_precipitation, 2m_temperature, potential_evaporation
era5_land_monthly_global.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information 2026

storm_v4_compact.source: derived from the event set storm_v4 (data/reference/event_sets.json) by services.loss.storm_events.compact

nfip_curve_claims.terms: This dataset is not intended to be an official federal report (FEMA)

copernicus_glo30_test.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Public (copernicus-dem-30m, AWS Open Data)
copernicus_glo30_test.kind: digital surface model (includes buildings and vegetation)
copernicus_glo30_test.licence_pointer: the bucket readme: 'available on a free basis for the general public under the terms and conditions of the Licence' at spacedata.copernicus.eu

aqueduct_floods_riverine.source: WRI Aqueduct Floods hazard maps, riverine inundation (aqueduct.wridata.org/AqueductFloods20)
aqueduct_floods_riverine.contents: inundation depth by return period: WATCH-forced baseline (1980) and RCP4.5/RCP8.5 2030/2050/2080 from five CMIP5 climate models; return periods 10, 100, 500 years
aqueduct_floods_riverine.licence_status: to read from WRI's terms before any use
aqueduct_floods_riverine.method_status: how the future maps are built: to read from WRI's method note before any use

jrc_huizinga_2017_flood_damage_functions.source: JRC Publications Repository, JRC105688: Huizinga, J., de Moel, H., Szewczyk, W. (2017). Global flood depth-damage functions. Methodology and the database with guidelines. EUR 28552 EN. doi:10.2760/16510
jrc_huizinga_2017_flood_damage_functions.approved: product owner (JRC flood curves, about 6 MB); fetched 2026-10-07 through the product owner's browser — the repository rejects automated requests
jrc_huizinga_2017_flood_damage_functions.licence: © European Union, 2017: 'The reuse of the document is authorised, provided the source is acknowledged and the original meaning or message of the texts are not distorted' (report, page ii)
jrc_huizinga_2017_flood_damage_functions.contents: report (PDF) and the database workbook (XLSX, 'European damage functions updated in October 2017'): fractional depth-damage functions for six classes × Europe, North America, Central & South America, Asia, Africa, Oceania and Global, with standard deviations for five regions; maximum damage per country

jrc_flood_europe.source: JRC / Copernicus EMS European river flood hazard maps (CEMS-EFAS flood_hazard), LISFLOOD-FP
jrc_flood_europe.contents: river flood depth (m) at return periods 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100, 200, 500 years, 3 arc-seconds; permanent water bodies and spurious-depth areas; README, CHANGELOG, copyright notice
jrc_flood_europe.licence_status: the folder's copyright notice is held beside the data; its terms are quoted into data/reference/hazard_intensity_layers.json before any use

jrc_flood_protection_europe.source: JRC PESETA IV floods collection — map of estimated flood defence standards in Europe (Dottori et al. 2022)
jrc_flood_protection_europe.contents: design return period (years) of local protection structures against river floods, 500 m GeoTIFF; the collection description; copyright notice
jrc_flood_protection_europe.licence_status: the folder's copyright notice is held beside the data; its terms are quoted into data/reference/hazard_intensity_layers.json before any use

natural_earth_admin1_10m.source: Natural Earth, Admin 1 – States, Provinces, 1:10m cultural vectors (naturalearthdata.com)
natural_earth_admin1_10m.attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
natural_earth_admin1_10m.version: Natural Earth 1:10m admin-1 (last modified Fri, 13 May 2022 05:20:49 GMT)

gdhy_v1_2_v1_3.source: Iizumi, T. (2019), Global dataset of historical yields v1.2 and v1.3 aligned version, PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.909132 (Iizumi & Sakai 2020, Scientific Data 7, 97)
gdhy_v1_2_v1_3.attribution: GDHY v1.2+v1.3 (Iizumi 2019; Iizumi & Sakai 2020), CC BY 4.0 — a cross-check only: modelled from satellite vegetation indices and FAO national statistics, never a calibration target
gdhy_v1_2_v1_3.version: GDHY v1.2 and v1.3 aligned version (last modified Tue, 28 Jan 2020 09:41:10 GMT)

climate_trace_assets.source: Climate TRACE asset-level sector packages (CO2e 100-year), downloads.climatetrace.org/latest
climate_trace_assets.contents: emissions sources (coordinates, capacity, emissions) and ownership chains (owner, owner LEI, share of the source) for the subsectors whose owners are mapped
climate_trace_assets.licence_status: the data guide: 'All Climate TRACE data is freely available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Public License, unless otherwise noted below' (ABOUT_THE_DATA/about_the_data_v5_10_0.pdf, held beside the data)

eea_industrial_sites.source: EEA Industrial Reporting under the IED 2010/75/EU and E-PRTR Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 — production facilities (Discodata, [IED].[latest])
eea_industrial_sites.query: SELECT id, localId, siteId, facilityName, parentCompanyName, parentCompanyURL, status, countryCode, x_4326, y_4326, EPRTRAnnexIMainActivity, facilityType, city, postalCode, reportingYear FROM [IED].[latest].[ProductionFacility] WHERE reportingYear = 2024 ORDER BY id
eea_industrial_sites.approved: product owner, 2026-10-23 (one query of the latest reporting year)
eea_industrial_sites.licence_status: the register's catalogue records (EEA SDI, version 16.0, February 2026): 'License CC-BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Copyright holder: European Environment Agency (EEA).'

aqueduct_floods_coastal.source: WRI Aqueduct Floods hazard maps, coastal inundation (aqueduct.wridata.org/AqueductFloods20)
aqueduct_floods_coastal.contents: inundation depth by return period (2–1,000 years), subsidence included: the present day (historical) and RCP4.5/RCP8.5 2030/2050/2080 at the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile of sea-level rise
aqueduct_floods_coastal.licence_status: verified: WRI's catalogue record (datasets.wri.org API, package aqueduct-floods-hazard-maps) states license_id 'cc-by' (2026-10-07, the riverine maps' record — one package)
